purpose: machine-readable ontology of engineering work-units for designing, diagnosing, and stabilizing loops in computing and learning systems (iteration/recursion, control-flow and resilience loops, learning/optimization loops, and coupling/cross-effects) as a subdomain node of systems thinking, feedback loops and control for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB; nodes are concrete, evaluable methods directly applicable to an orchestrated-specialist system's own training and eval loops.
assumptions: Computational & Learning Loops is modeled as a subdomain of systems thinking, feedback loops and control.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable engineering work-units for loops, not generic CS or ML topics.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope spans theory-of-computation iteration/termination (Sipser), cybernetic feedback/control (Wiener), and distributed-systems resilience patterns (retry-with-backoff, circuit breaker, idempotency).
exclusions: General algorithm design and data structures except as they shape loop correctness and cost.
Full distributed-systems architecture (consensus, storage, networking) beyond resilience-loop patterns.
Model architecture and feature engineering except where they form part of a training/eval loop.
Hardware-level pipelines and instruction-level loop optimization.

competency_questions.question: What loops exist in this system, and how is each classified by type, period, and stability class?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOOP_IDENTIFICATION yields a classified loop inventory

competency_questions.question: What invariant establishes a given loop's correctness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOOP_INVARIANTS provides a proven invariant implying the postcondition

competency_questions.question: Does this loop terminate, and if termination is undecidable, what operational bound applies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERMINATION_HALTING gives a ranking function or an explicit cap

competency_questions.question: Will this iterative process converge, and to what fixed point at what rate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONVERGENCE_FIXED_POINTS states the contraction condition and rate

competency_questions.question: What is the time/space complexity contributed by this loop or recursion?
How should the event/run loop schedule tasks to avoid starvation and overload?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVENT_LOOP and LOOP_OBSERVABILITY define scheduling, backpressure, and metrics

competency_questions.question: How are retries, rate limits, and breakers configured so transient failures recover without amplifying load?
How are retried/replayed operations made safe against double-applied effects?
How is the optimization loop tuned for stable convergence and divergence diagnosed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GRADIENT_DESCENT defines schedule and divergence diagnosis

competency_questions.question: How does evaluation steer training, and when does the loop stop or roll back on regression?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_IN_LOOP and EARLY_STOPPING_ROLLBACK define eval cadence and rollback

competency_questions.question: How is the reward/feedback signal designed to resist gaming and stay aligned to the true objective?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REWARD_FEEDBACK_SIGNAL specifies alignment and gaming checks

competency_questions.question: Which couplings are stabilizing vs amplifying, and what is each loop's gain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FEEDBACK_POLARITY signs polarity and estimates loop gain

competency_questions.question: How far can a local failure cascade, and how is the blast radius bounded and stabilized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CASCADE_AMPLIFICATION, STABILITY_DAMPING and STABILIZATION_DECISION bound and fix it

competency_questions.question: How is model-collapse feedback from self-training detected and broken?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODEL_COLLAPSE_FEEDBACK provides provenance anchoring and diversity monitoring

glossary.definition: a control structure or process that repeats a body until a condition or signal halts it
a predicate true before and after every iteration that, with the guard, implies the postcondition
the property that a loop's execution ends in finite steps under all admissible inputs
a state mapped to itself by the iteration map, the target an iterative process converges toward
increasing the delay between successive retries, typically exponentially with jitter
a state machine that trips open on sustained downstream failure to fail fast and stop cascades
the property that applying an operation once or many times yields the same final state
the sign of a loop: negative feedback stabilizes, positive feedback amplifies
the propagation and amplification of a local failure or signal across coupled loops
degradation and diversity loss when a model is iteratively trained on model-generated data
the optimizer exploiting a proxy reward to score high while failing the true objective
adding smoothing, hysteresis, or deadbands to suppress oscillation and stabilize a loop

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from theory-of-computation and control/cybernetics literature (Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation; Wiener, Cybernetics) and standard distributed-systems resilience patterns (retry-with-backoff, circuit breaker, idempotency); no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Identify and classify every loop in a system (iteration, recursion, control-flow, learning, feedback) and tag its purpose, period, and stability class before any analysis or fix.

included: period and trigger of each loop

contradictors: engineer who fixes a symptom without locating the driving loop

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new loop or coupling is discovered that was not in the inventory

pros.claim: a complete loop inventory prevents fixing the wrong loop
pros.example: cascading retries traced to an outer loop, not the failing call

pros.claim: classification routes each loop to the right stability tool
pros.example: a learning loop sent to convergence analysis, a control loop to backoff design

cons.claim: inventory can miss implicit or emergent loops
cons.example: a feedback loop formed only at runtime through shared state

failure_modes: implicit loops via shared state go uncatalogued
async loops misclassified as independent
acceptance_tests: every executable loop appears in the inventory with a class tag
each loop has a named trigger and period
revisit_triggers: new component added to the pipeline
an incident reveals an uncatalogued loop

nodes.definition: State and prove the loop invariant: a predicate true before and after each iteration that, with the exit condition, establishes the loop's correctness.
contradictors: coder who trusts tests instead of an invariant

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: loop body or guard is modified

pros.claim: an invariant turns ad hoc reasoning into a checkable correctness proof
pros.example: a sum-accumulation invariant proves the result regardless of input size

pros.claim: invariants double as runtime assertions
pros.example: asserting the invariant each iteration catches corruption early

cons.claim: finding a strong-enough invariant can be hard
cons.example: nested loops needing a conjoined invariant over both indices

failure_modes: invariant too weak to imply the postcondition
invariant not preserved on an edge iteration
acceptance_tests: invariant holds at init, is maintained, and with the guard implies the postcondition
invariant checked as a runtime assertion on a sample run

nodes.definition: Prove loop termination via a decreasing well-founded ranking function and reason about when termination is undecidable (the halting problem) and must be bounded operationally.
contradictors: engineer who assumes a loop always terminates

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a loop's exit condition depends on external or adversarial input

pros.claim: a ranking function gives a hard termination guarantee
pros.example: a strictly decreasing nonnegative counter proves the loop ends

pros.claim: recognizing undecidability forces an explicit operational bound
pros.example: capping iterations because no general termination proof exists

cons.claim: general termination is undecidable; proofs are case-specific
cons.example: a collatz-like loop with no known ranking function

failure_modes: unbounded loop on adversarial input
ranking function not actually decreasing on all paths
acceptance_tests: a well-founded decreasing measure is exhibited or an explicit iteration cap is set
worst-case input cannot run the loop unbounded

nodes.definition: Analyze iterative processes as maps toward a fixed point: establish existence, the contraction/stability condition, and the rate of convergence to the fixed point.
contradictors: engineer who iterates without checking the convergence condition

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the update map or its operating point changes

pros.claim: a contraction condition guarantees convergence to a unique fixed point
pros.example: Banach contraction bounds the error each iteration

pros.claim: convergence rate sets a defensible iteration budget
pros.example: quadratic convergence justifies few iterations to tolerance

cons.claim: non-contractive maps can oscillate or diverge
cons.example: fixed-point iteration with derivative magnitude above one diverges

failure_modes: divergence when the contraction condition fails
stopping at a spurious near-stationary point
acceptance_tests: the contraction/stability condition is checked before iterating
a stopping rule tied to the convergence metric is defined
revisit_triggers: operating point moves outside the contraction region

nodes.definition: Derive the time and space complexity contributed by loops and recursion (nesting, recurrences, amortization) to predict cost growth and locate hotspots.
contradictors: engineer who profiles before bounding the asymptotics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: input-size regime or data structure changes

pros.claim: asymptotic bounds predict scaling before load testing
pros.example: a triple-nested loop flagged as cubic before deployment

pros.claim: amortized analysis justifies cheap average cost despite costly steps
pros.example: dynamic-array growth amortized to O(1) per append

cons.claim: asymptotics hide constants that dominate at real sizes
cons.example: an O(n log n) routine slower than O(n^2) for small n

failure_modes: hidden quadratic from an inner loop on a data structure
stack overflow from unbounded recursion depth
acceptance_tests: a closed-form or asymptotic bound is given for each loop nest
recurrences are solved, not guessed

nodes.definition: Decide between recursion and iteration and transform between them (tail-call elimination, explicit stack, memoization) for correctness, stack safety, and performance.
contradictors: coder who recurses deeply on bounded stacks

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recursion depth approaches the stack limit at scale

pros.claim: iterative form removes stack-overflow risk
pros.example: converting deep tree recursion to an explicit stack

pros.claim: memoization collapses exponential recursion to polynomial
pros.example: top-down DP caches overlapping subproblems

cons.claim: manual conversion can introduce off-by-one or state-tracking bugs
cons.example: an explicit-stack rewrite that visits a node twice

failure_modes: stack overflow on deep recursion
memo invalidation bug returns stale results
acceptance_tests: transformed loop is verified equivalent to the original on test cases
stack depth is bounded under worst-case input

nodes.definition: Design and reason about the event/run loop that drives asynchronous systems: task scheduling, fairness, backpressure, and starvation avoidance.
contradictors: developer who blocks the event loop with sync work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new blocking task type or load class enters the loop

pros.claim: a fair scheduler prevents starvation under load
pros.example: weighted-fair queuing keeps low-priority tasks progressing

pros.claim: backpressure protects the loop from overload collapse
pros.example: bounded queues shed or pause producers before melting down

cons.claim: a blocked event loop stalls the whole system
cons.example: a synchronous file read freezing all pending tasks

failure_modes: event loop blocked by synchronous work
starvation of low-priority tasks
unbounded queue growth
acceptance_tests: no task class can be starved indefinitely under sustained load
backpressure engages before queue memory is exhausted

nodes.definition: Design retry policy with exponential backoff and jitter, bounded attempts, and retry-budgets so transient failures recover without synchronized retry storms.
contradictors: engineer who retries immediately and unbounded

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a downstream dependency's failure profile or capacity changes

pros.claim: backoff with jitter prevents synchronized retry storms
pros.example: jittered exponential backoff de-correlates client retries

pros.claim: bounded attempts and retry budgets cap amplification
pros.example: a retry budget stops one failure from tripling load

cons.claim: naive retries amplify load and turn a blip into an outage
cons.example: immediate unlimited retries DDoSing a recovering service

failure_modes: retry storm amplifies a transient failure
retrying non-idempotent operations causes duplicates
unbounded retries never terminate
acceptance_tests: retries are bounded and jittered, with a retry budget
only retryable, idempotent operations are retried
revisit_triggers: failure rate of a dependency rises
retry budget is exhausted in production

nodes.definition: Bound the rate of a loop or request stream (token/leaky bucket, concurrency caps) to protect shared resources and enforce fairness and quotas.
contradictors: engineer who lets a loop run at unbounded rate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: downstream capacity or client mix changes materially

pros.claim: rate limits protect shared resources from overload
pros.example: a token bucket caps writes to a database under bursts

pros.claim: quotas enforce fairness across clients
pros.example: per-tenant limits stop one client starving others

cons.claim: limits set too tight throttle legitimate load
cons.example: a low global cap rejecting valid traffic during a spike

failure_modes: limit too tight rejects valid work
limit too loose fails to protect the resource
global limit ignores per-client fairness
acceptance_tests: sustained load above capacity is shed or queued, not passed through
per-client fairness holds under a noisy-neighbor test

nodes.definition: Implement a circuit breaker that trips open on sustained downstream failure, fails fast, and probes for recovery via a half-open state to stop cascading failures.
contradictors: engineer who keeps calling a failing dependency

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a downstream dependency's failure correlation or recovery time changes

pros.claim: a breaker stops a failing dependency from cascading
pros.example: tripping open sheds load and lets the dependency recover

pros.claim: half-open probing restores service without a thundering herd
pros.example: a single probe confirms recovery before reopening traffic

cons.claim: a mis-tuned breaker flaps or stays open too long
cons.example: a tight threshold tripping on normal transient errors

failure_modes: breaker flapping between open and closed
threshold so loose it never trips
half-open probe storms the recovering service
acceptance_tests: sustained downstream failure trips the breaker within the configured window
half-open allows a single probe, not a herd

nodes.definition: Make retried and replayed loop operations safe via idempotency keys, dedup, and effectively-once semantics so repeats do not double-apply effects.
contradictors: engineer who assumes operations run exactly once

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an operation gains a non-idempotent side effect

pros.claim: idempotency makes retries and replays safe
pros.example: an idempotency key prevents a double charge on retry

pros.claim: effectively-once is achievable from at-least-once + dedup
pros.example: dedup on a message id collapses redelivery

cons.claim: dedup windows and key collisions can still admit duplicates
cons.example: a too-short dedup TTL letting a late retry double-apply

failure_modes: double-applied side effect from a retried non-idempotent op
dedup window too short
key collision merges distinct operations
acceptance_tests: replaying any operation produces the same final state as one application
a forced duplicate is rejected by the dedup store
revisit_triggers: a new side-effecting operation is added
dedup window or key scheme changes

nodes.definition: Analyze the optimization loop: learning-rate and schedule choice, descent/convergence conditions, and divergence/oscillation diagnosis for gradient-based training.
contradictors: practitioner who sets the learning rate by guesswork

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: loss diverges, plateaus, or oscillates during training

pros.claim: a sound learning-rate schedule is the main driver of stable convergence
pros.example: warmup plus decay stabilizes early training and sharpens late convergence

pros.claim: reading the loss curve diagnoses divergence vs plateau early
pros.example: a rising loss flags too-high learning rate before wasted compute

cons.claim: too-high a rate diverges; too-low wastes compute and stalls
cons.example: loss exploding to NaN from an aggressive learning rate

failure_modes: divergence to NaN from an excessive learning rate
oscillation around a minimum
silent stall in a flat region
acceptance_tests: loss decreases and stabilizes within the compute budget on a validation metric
no NaN/inf appears in the training loop

nodes.definition: Couple evaluation into the training loop: hold-out/online eval cadence, metric selection, and leakage prevention so learning is steered by trustworthy signal.
contradictors: practitioner who tunes on the test set

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the eval metric stops correlating with the true objective

pros.claim: eval in the loop catches regressions while they are cheap to fix
pros.example: a per-epoch eval flags a quality drop before full training spend

pros.claim: leakage-free splits keep the steering signal honest
pros.example: strict train/eval separation prevents optimistic metrics

cons.claim: a leaked or gameable metric steers learning the wrong way
cons.example: tuning on the test set inflating reported accuracy

failure_modes: train/eval leakage inflates metrics
eval metric diverges from the true objective
eval cadence too sparse to catch regressions
acceptance_tests: train and eval splits are provably disjoint
the eval metric is shown to track the target objective on a probe set

nodes.definition: Stop or roll back the learning loop on validated regression: patience-based early stopping, best-checkpoint selection, and rollback gates against a known-good baseline.
contradictors: practitioner who ships the last checkpoint regardless of eval

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a deployed model regresses against the known-good baseline

pros.claim: rollback on regression bounds the blast radius of a bad update
pros.example: reverting to the last good checkpoint restores quality immediately

pros.claim: early stopping prevents overfitting and wasted compute
pros.example: stopping at best-val checkpoint avoids late-epoch overfit

cons.claim: too-eager stopping abandons a still-improving run
cons.example: stopping during a temporary plateau before a later drop

failure_modes: no rollback path leaves a regression in production
early stop fires on a transient plateau
best-checkpoint selection uses a leaked metric
acceptance_tests: a regression beyond threshold triggers rollback to a known-good baseline
the selected checkpoint beats the baseline on the eval metric
revisit_triggers: a rollback fails to restore quality

nodes.definition: Design the reward/feedback signal that closes a learning loop so it is aligned, robust to gaming, and not reward-hacked or shortcut by the optimizer.

included: alignment of proxy to true goal

contradictors: practitioner who optimizes a proxy and ignores Goodhart

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the optimizer finds a high-reward, low-true-value behavior

pros.claim: an aligned reward keeps the loop optimizing the real goal
pros.example: a reward tied to held-out quality resists shortcut behavior

pros.claim: explicit gaming checks catch reward hacking early
pros.example: a probe for degenerate high-reward outputs flags hacking

cons.claim: a proxy reward invites Goodharting and reward hacking
cons.example: optimizing click-rate degrading actual content quality

failure_modes: reward hacking exploits a proxy
misaligned signal optimizes the wrong behavior
reward sparsity stalls learning
acceptance_tests: high-reward outputs are audited for alignment with the true objective
a known gaming strategy does not score well under the reward

nodes.definition: Classify feedback polarity across coupled pipeline stages: negative feedback that stabilizes vs positive feedback that amplifies, and trace each loop's gain.
contradictors: engineer who treats coupled stages as independent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a coupling's sign or gain changes with the operating point

pros.claim: polarity tells you whether a loop self-corrects or runs away
pros.example: a negative-feedback controller damps a transient automatically

pros.claim: loop-gain estimates predict instability before it manifests
pros.example: gain above unity flags an amplifying loop to be broken

cons.claim: polarity can flip with operating point or saturation
cons.example: a stabilizing loop turning amplifying once a buffer saturates

failure_modes: unrecognized positive feedback runs away
sign error damps the wrong loop
gain estimated at the wrong operating point
acceptance_tests: every coupling is signed and its loop gain estimated
amplifying loops are flagged for damping or breaking
revisit_triggers: a new coupling edge is added

nodes.definition: Analyze how a local failure or signal cascades and amplifies across coupled loops, and design isolation (bulkheads, damping, breaking points) to bound the blast radius.
contradictors: engineer who hardens one node and ignores propagation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a near-miss or incident reveals an unbounded cascade path

pros.claim: bulkheads bound a failure to one partition
pros.example: isolating a tenant pool stops one failure spreading system-wide

pros.claim: amplification analysis sizes the worst-case blast radius
pros.example: estimating a 5x retry amplification before it hits production

cons.claim: hidden coupling can create cascades isolation misses
cons.example: a shared cache linking supposedly isolated services

failure_modes: local failure cascades system-wide
amplification underestimated
isolation boundary leaks through shared state
acceptance_tests: a single-component failure is bounded to its partition in a fault-injection test
worst-case amplification factor is estimated and capped
revisit_triggers: a new coupling or shared resource appears
an incident exceeds the predicted blast radius

nodes.definition: Detect and break the self-training feedback loop in which a model trained on its own (or other models') outputs degrades, loses tail diversity, and collapses over generations.
contradictors: practitioner who recycles synthetic outputs as training data unchecked

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: training data ingests model-generated content without provenance

pros.claim: anchoring on real data breaks the collapse loop
pros.example: blending verified human data each generation preserves the tails

pros.claim: diversity monitoring detects collapse before it is irreversible
pros.example: tracking output entropy flags early variance loss

cons.claim: collapse can be gradual and hard to detect until tails are lost
cons.example: successive generations quietly narrowing to a few modes

failure_modes: models train on their own outputs and degrade
tail diversity lost irreversibly
synthetic data contaminates the training set without provenance
acceptance_tests: training-data provenance distinguishes real from model-generated content
output diversity does not monotonically collapse across generations on a probe

nodes.definition: Stabilize an unstable or oscillating loop by adding damping, hysteresis, deadbands, smoothing, or controller tuning while preserving responsiveness.
contradictors: engineer who reacts to every fluctuation without damping

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a loop begins oscillating or hunting in production

pros.claim: damping converts oscillation into smooth settling
pros.example: adding hysteresis stops an autoscaler from flapping

pros.claim: deadbands suppress reaction to noise
pros.example: ignoring sub-threshold changes prevents needless churn

cons.claim: over-damping makes the loop sluggish and slow to react
cons.example: too much smoothing delaying response to a real spike

failure_modes: sustained oscillation or hunting
over-damping kills responsiveness
hysteresis band mis-sized
acceptance_tests: the loop settles without sustained oscillation under a step input
responsiveness stays within the required latency after damping

nodes.definition: Instrument loops for observability: per-loop metrics (iteration count, latency, convergence, retry/trip rates), tracing, and alerts so loop pathologies are detectable.
contradictors: engineer who runs loops blind without metrics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a loop pathology occurs that existing telemetry could not detect

pros.claim: per-loop metrics make pathologies detectable and alertable
pros.example: a retry-rate spike alert catches a storm before outage

pros.claim: tracing localizes which loop in a chain misbehaves
pros.example: span data isolates the amplifying loop in a cascade

cons.claim: excessive instrumentation adds overhead and noise
cons.example: high-cardinality per-iteration metrics overwhelming the pipeline

failure_modes: loop pathology invisible without instrumentation
alert fatigue from noisy metrics
high-cardinality telemetry overload
acceptance_tests: each catalogued loop emits at least one health metric with an alert threshold
a seeded pathology fires the corresponding alert
revisit_triggers: new loop added to the inventory

nodes.definition: Decide the stabilization strategy for a diagnosed loop pathology: break the loop, add backoff/limit/breaker, add damping, or rearchitect, weighing reversibility and risk.
contradictors: engineer who applies a fix without weighing cross-effects

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a stabilization intervention has unexpected cross-effects

pros.claim: a deliberate strategy avoids fixes that shift the problem elsewhere
pros.example: choosing a breaker over more retries actually halts the cascade

pros.claim: reversibility weighting protects against irreversible mistakes
pros.example: preferring a reversible bound over a one-way rearchitecture

cons.claim: a wrong intervention can move or worsen the instability
cons.example: adding retries that amplify the very cascade being fixed

failure_modes: intervention shifts instability to another loop
irreversible change made without review
fix verified only locally, not system-wide
acceptance_tests: the chosen intervention is validated against the full coupling map, not one loop
irreversible interventions carry a human-review decision record
revisit_triggers: an incident recurs after the fix

edges.why_related: a loop must be located and classified before an invariant can be stated for it
edges.benefit_of_coupling: invariant work targets a real, scoped loop
edges.risk_of_conflict: proving an invariant for a misidentified loop wastes effort
edges.example: writing an invariant for the wrong nested loop
edges.resolution_rule: identify and classify the loop before stating its invariant

edges.why_related: termination is reasoned per identified loop and its guard
edges.benefit_of_coupling: termination proofs are scoped to catalogued loops
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing a loop leaves an unbounded path unanalyzed
edges.example: an uncatalogued async loop never bounded
edges.resolution_rule: catalogue loops before proving termination

edges.why_related: convergence analysis applies to identified iterative maps
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fixed-point analysis targets the right iteration
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing convergence of a misclassified loop misleads
edges.example: treating a control loop as an optimizer
edges.resolution_rule: classify the loop type before convergence analysis

edges.why_related: complexity is bounded per loop and recursion structure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cost bounds attach to real loop nests
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing a loop hides a cost driver
edges.example: an inner loop on a structure missed in the bound
edges.resolution_rule: inventory loops before complexity analysis

edges.why_related: complexity informs whether to convert recursion to iteration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: transform decisions are cost-justified
edges.risk_of_conflict: converting without cost analysis can regress performance
edges.example: memoizing where it adds overhead
edges.resolution_rule: analyze complexity before choosing recursion vs iteration

edges.why_related: the driving event loop must be identified before its scheduling is designed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scheduling work targets the real run loop
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing for the wrong loop misallocates effort
edges.example: tuning a worker pool that is not the bottleneck loop
edges.resolution_rule: identify the driving loop before scheduling design

edges.why_related: the loop/stream to bound must be identified before limits are set
edges.benefit_of_coupling: limits attach to the real request loop
edges.risk_of_conflict: limiting the wrong stage misses the overload source
edges.example: throttling a cheap stage while the costly loop runs free
edges.resolution_rule: identify the loop before rate-limiting it

edges.why_related: couplings must be inventoried before their feedback polarity is signed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: polarity is assigned to real coupling edges
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing a coupling hides an amplifying loop
edges.example: an unsigned shared-state coupling running away
edges.resolution_rule: inventory couplings before signing polarity

edges.why_related: loops must be catalogued before they can be instrumented
edges.benefit_of_coupling: instrumentation covers every catalogued loop
edges.risk_of_conflict: an uninstrumented loop hides its pathology
edges.example: a retry loop with no metric emitting silently
edges.resolution_rule: inventory loops before instrumenting them

edges.why_related: retry loops need a termination/iteration bound to avoid running forever
edges.benefit_of_coupling: retries inherit a hard attempt bound
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded retries never terminate
edges.example: infinite retries against a permanently-down service
edges.resolution_rule: bound retry attempts using termination reasoning

edges.why_related: gradient descent is a fixed-point/convergence process and inherits its conditions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: training stability rests on convergence theory
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the convergence condition risks divergence
edges.example: a learning rate violating the descent condition
edges.resolution_rule: apply convergence conditions before tuning the optimizer

edges.why_related: evaluation is coupled into the running optimization loop
edges.benefit_of_coupling: eval steers a converging training run
edges.risk_of_conflict: eval without a stable training loop is noisy
edges.example: evaluating a diverging run produces meaningless metrics
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize the optimization loop before eval-in-loop

edges.why_related: stopping/rollback decisions consume the eval-in-loop signal
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stop/rollback acts on trustworthy eval
edges.risk_of_conflict: stopping on a leaked metric is wrong
edges.example: rolling back based on a leaked eval score
edges.resolution_rule: secure eval integrity before stop/rollback

edges.why_related: reward design relies on a trustworthy eval signal to detect gaming
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reward audits use the eval harness
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing reward without honest eval invites hacking
edges.example: a reward validated only on a gameable metric
edges.resolution_rule: establish honest eval before finalizing the reward

edges.why_related: a breaker complements retries by tripping when retries keep failing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: retries plus a breaker bound amplification
edges.risk_of_conflict: retries without a breaker can hammer a down service
edges.example: endless backoff retries with no trip condition
edges.resolution_rule: pair bounded retries with a circuit breaker

edges.why_related: retried operations must be idempotent to be safe to repeat
edges.benefit_of_coupling: retries become safe under idempotency
edges.risk_of_conflict: retrying non-idempotent ops double-applies effects
edges.example: a retried payment charging twice
edges.resolution_rule: make operations idempotent before enabling retries

edges.why_related: amplifying (positive) feedback is the mechanism of cascades
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cascade analysis builds on polarity/gain
edges.risk_of_conflict: cascades are unpredictable without polarity
edges.example: an unsigned amplifying loop causing a runaway
edges.resolution_rule: sign feedback polarity before cascade analysis

edges.why_related: damping is applied to loops whose polarity/gain make them unstable
edges.benefit_of_coupling: damping targets the unstable loops
edges.risk_of_conflict: damping the wrong loop wastes margin
edges.example: adding hysteresis to a stable loop while the unstable one runs
edges.resolution_rule: identify unstable loops via polarity before damping

edges.why_related: stability/contraction analysis informs damping parameter choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: damping is tuned from stability margins
edges.risk_of_conflict: damping set without stability analysis can over- or under-damp
edges.example: guessing a smoothing constant
edges.resolution_rule: derive stability margins before setting damping

edges.why_related: retry behavior changes the amplification factor of a cascade
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tuned retries reduce cascade gain
edges.risk_of_conflict: aggressive retries raise the cascade amplification
edges.example: a retry storm multiplying load fivefold downstream
edges.resolution_rule: cap retries and budgets to keep cascade gain bounded

edges.why_related: a breaker lowers the probability and reach of a cascade
edges.benefit_of_coupling: breakers shrink the blast radius
edges.risk_of_conflict: a missing breaker lets failure propagate
edges.example: no breaker so one outage takes the fleet down
edges.resolution_rule: place breakers at cascade choke points

edges.why_related: eval-in-loop detects diversity collapse from self-training
edges.benefit_of_coupling: collapse is caught while reversible
edges.risk_of_conflict: without eval, collapse is found too late
edges.example: diversity loss noticed only after generations
edges.resolution_rule: monitor diversity in eval to detect collapse early

edges.why_related: model collapse is a positive-feedback self-consumption loop
edges.benefit_of_coupling: polarity framing explains the collapse mechanism
edges.risk_of_conflict: mis-signing the loop misses the runaway
edges.example: treating self-training as neutral rather than amplifying
edges.resolution_rule: sign the self-training loop as positive feedback

edges.why_related: stabilization decisions need observability to diagnose and verify
edges.benefit_of_coupling: decisions are grounded in loop telemetry
edges.risk_of_conflict: fixing blind risks the wrong intervention
edges.example: choosing a fix without metrics to confirm it
edges.resolution_rule: instrument the loop before deciding the fix

edges.why_related: the cascade analysis sizes the problem the decision must address
edges.benefit_of_coupling: intervention is scoped to the real blast radius
edges.risk_of_conflict: deciding without cascade scope under-fixes
edges.example: a local fix that ignores the cascade path
edges.resolution_rule: size the cascade before choosing the intervention

edges.why_related: damping is one candidate the stabilization decision weighs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: damping is compared against other interventions
edges.risk_of_conflict: jumping to damping skips better options
edges.example: damping a loop that should be broken instead
edges.resolution_rule: weigh damping among all interventions in the decision

edges.why_related: a chosen intervention can reveal or create new loops to re-inventory
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the loop inventory stays current after fixes
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale inventory after a fix hides new loops
edges.example: a new retry loop introduced by the fix itself
edges.resolution_rule: re-run loop identification after each stabilization; stop when the inventory is stable

edges.why_related: a rollback triggers re-running the training loop from a good checkpoint
edges.benefit_of_coupling: training resumes from a known-good state
edges.risk_of_conflict: without a trigger, regressions persist
edges.example: restarting training after a rollback
edges.resolution_rule: resume training on rollback; stop when eval beats the baseline

edges.why_related: detected collapse triggers revisiting eval and data provenance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: eval and data hygiene are revisited on collapse signal
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring collapse signals lets degradation compound
edges.example: tightening provenance after a diversity drop
edges.resolution_rule: revisit eval/provenance on collapse signal; stop when diversity stabilizes

edges.why_related: rate limits bound the admission rate the event loop must service
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the event loop is protected from overload
edges.risk_of_conflict: limits too tight starve the loop of work
edges.example: admission control shaping the loop's input
edges.resolution_rule: tune limits so the loop is protected but not starved

edges.why_related: rate limits bound the rate at which retries may be issued
edges.benefit_of_coupling: retries respect the global rate budget
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded retries can blow the rate budget
edges.example: a retry budget consuming the rate limit
edges.resolution_rule: subordinate retry rate to the global rate limit

edges.why_related: idempotency bounds what side effects breaker-driven replays may cause
edges.benefit_of_coupling: breaker fallbacks/replays stay side-effect-safe
edges.risk_of_conflict: non-idempotent fallback duplicates effects
edges.example: a fallback replay double-writing
edges.resolution_rule: require idempotent operations on breaker fallback paths

edges.why_related: tight convergence tolerance fights with a small iteration/termination budget
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balancing accuracy against bounded iterations
edges.risk_of_conflict: chasing tolerance can blow the iteration cap
edges.example: lowering tolerance until the loop never hits the cap
edges.resolution_rule: cap iterations; accept the best feasible tolerance within the budget

edges.why_related: more retries improve recovery but push against the rate/limit budget
edges.benefit_of_coupling: recovery vs resource protection are balanced
edges.risk_of_conflict: aggressive retries breach limits and overload
edges.example: a recovery push tripping the rate limiter
edges.resolution_rule: rate limit dominates; retries fit inside the remaining budget

edges.why_related: more training iterations vs stopping early to avoid overfit/regression
edges.benefit_of_coupling: training progress vs regression safety are traded
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-training overfits; over-eager stopping underfits
edges.example: stopping a still-improving run vs overfitting a long one
edges.resolution_rule: stop on validated regression; otherwise continue within the compute budget

edges.why_related: optimizing the reward proxy can diverge from the honest eval objective
edges.benefit_of_coupling: proxy optimization vs true-objective fidelity are balanced
edges.risk_of_conflict: reward hacking inflates proxy while eval truth drops
edges.example: click-reward rising while quality eval falls
edges.resolution_rule: when proxy and eval diverge, the eval objective dominates

edges.why_related: damping for stability reduces the loop's responsiveness/throughput
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stability vs responsiveness are balanced
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-damping makes the loop sluggish
edges.example: smoothing that delays reaction to a real spike
edges.resolution_rule: damp only enough to meet the stability margin; preserve the latency SLO

edges.why_related: using cheap model-generated data speeds training but risks collapse
edges.benefit_of_coupling: data scale vs distributional integrity are balanced
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthetic recycling collapses the distribution
edges.example: training on self-output for volume at the cost of diversity
edges.resolution_rule: anchor on real data; bound synthetic share to protect diversity

edges.why_related: both are admission/flow-control resilience patterns on request loops
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared resilience tooling and mental model
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them blurs distinct responsibilities
edges.example: treating a limiter as a retry policy
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct: backoff governs re-attempts, limiting governs admission

edges.why_related: both reason about iterative stability and settling behavior
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared stability vocabulary across CS and control
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-merging hides the analysis-vs-intervention split
edges.example: using a convergence proof as if it were a damping fix
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct: convergence analyzes, damping intervenes

conflict_axes.trigger: a tighter tolerance demands more iterations than the budget allows
resolution_order: fix the hard iteration/time budget
take the best feasible tolerance within it
record residual error as a limitation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the operational iteration budget bounds the loop; accuracy is maximized within it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: required accuracy is unreachable within any safe iteration cap
conflict_axes.example: a solver that would need unbounded iterations to hit tolerance

conflict_axes.trigger: aggressive retries to recover collide with limits protecting the resource
resolution_order: enforce the protective limit/breaker
fit retries inside the remaining budget
fail fast when budget is exhausted
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: resource protection (limit/breaker) dominates; recovery operates within the protected budget
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: retries needed for recovery would require breaching the protection limit
conflict_axes.example: a retry storm threatening a recovering database

conflict_axes.trigger: continuing to train risks overfit/regression while stopping risks underfitting
resolution_order: evaluate against the known-good baseline
stop or roll back on validated regression
otherwise continue within the compute budget
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validated regression against baseline dominates; absent it, training continues
conflict_axes.example: deciding whether a late-epoch dip is overfit or noise

conflict_axes.trigger: the optimizer raises the reward proxy while the true-objective eval drops
resolution_order: detect proxy-eval divergence
treat the true-objective eval as authoritative
revise the reward to penalize the gaming
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the true-objective eval dominates the proxy reward when they diverge
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: reward hacking is suspected on a high-stakes objective
conflict_axes.example: engagement reward climbing as quality eval falls

conflict_axes.trigger: damping added for stability slows the loop's reaction to real changes
resolution_order: set the minimum stability margin required
add only enough damping to meet it
verify the latency SLO still holds
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: meet the stability margin first, then minimize damping to protect responsiveness
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: no damping satisfies both stability and the latency SLO
conflict_axes.example: an autoscaler smoothed until it lags demand

conflict_axes.trigger: recycling cheap model-generated data for scale risks distributional collapse
resolution_order: track data provenance
bound the synthetic share
anchor each generation on verified real data
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: distributional integrity dominates; synthetic data is bounded and provenance-tracked
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: synthetic share rises with no real-data anchor
conflict_axes.example: a pipeline training mostly on prior model outputs

conflict_axes.trigger: a fix that stabilizes one loop destabilizes or overloads a coupled loop
resolution_order: evaluate the intervention against the full coupling map
prefer fixes that bound global blast radius
escalate irreversible global changes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: global stability dominates a locally-optimal fix
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the only local fix shifts instability to a critical coupled loop
conflict_axes.example: adding retries that fix one call but amplify a cascade

conflict_axes.trigger: a loop cannot be formally proven terminating/correct yet must ship with operational guards
resolution_order: attempt the proof/invariant
where undecidable, add operational caps and timeouts
document the residual risk
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prefer a proof; where impossible, operational bounds plus monitoring dominate unbounded execution
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: neither a proof nor a safe operational bound is available
conflict_axes.example: an external-input loop with no provable termination

conflict_axes.trigger: per-iteration instrumentation adds overhead to a hot loop
resolution_order: identify the minimal health signals needed
sample or aggregate high-cardinality metrics
keep overhead within the loop's budget
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: keep enough instrumentation to detect known pathologies; trim the rest to protect the loop budget
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: required telemetry overhead violates the loop's latency budget
conflict_axes.example: high-cardinality per-iteration metrics slowing a training step

edge_cases.trigger: a retry loop has no attempt cap or termination bound
edge_cases.failure_mode: infinite retries against a persistently failing dependency
edge_cases.example: a client retrying a 500 forever with no max attempts
edge_cases.detection_method: static check for retry loops lacking a max-attempt/budget bound
resolution: add a max-attempt and retry budget
add jittered backoff and a circuit breaker

edge_cases.trigger: synchronized clients retry without jitter during a partial outage
edge_cases.failure_mode: retry storm amplifies a transient failure into an outage
edge_cases.example: all clients retrying on the same schedule overwhelming a recovering service
edge_cases.detection_method: alert on retry-rate and load correlation spikes during failures
resolution: add jitter and retry budgets
trip a circuit breaker
apply rate limiting

edge_cases.trigger: a non-idempotent operation is retried after an ambiguous timeout
edge_cases.example: a payment retried on timeout charging the customer twice
edge_cases.detection_method: audit retried operations for idempotency keys and dedup
resolution: add idempotency keys and a dedup store
make the operation effectively-once

edge_cases.trigger: breaker thresholds are mis-tuned around the normal error rate
edge_cases.example: a tight threshold tripping on normal transient errors then resetting
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor breaker state-transition frequency for flapping
resolution: add hysteresis between trip and reset thresholds
widen the failure window

edge_cases.trigger: learning rate violates the descent/contraction condition
edge_cases.failure_mode: loss diverges to NaN and the run is wasted
edge_cases.example: an aggressive learning rate exploding the loss to NaN
edge_cases.detection_method: detect rising loss or NaN/inf in the training loop and halt
resolution: reduce the learning rate or add warmup
add gradient clipping

edge_cases.trigger: train and eval data overlap or the test set is tuned on
edge_cases.example: selecting a checkpoint on a metric leaked from training
edge_cases.detection_method: verify train/eval split disjointness and freeze the test set
resolution: enforce disjoint splits
hold out a sealed test set

edge_cases.trigger: the optimizer finds a high-reward, low-true-value behavior
edge_cases.failure_mode: reward hacking degrades the real objective
edge_cases.example: maximizing a click proxy while content quality falls
edge_cases.detection_method: compare proxy reward trend against the true-objective eval for divergence
resolution: treat the true-objective eval as authoritative
penalize the gaming pattern in the reward

edge_cases.trigger: training data ingests model-generated content without provenance
edge_cases.failure_mode: successive generations lose tail diversity and collapse
edge_cases.example: a model quietly narrowing to a few modes over generations
edge_cases.detection_method: track output diversity/entropy generation-over-generation against a real-data probe
resolution: anchor on verified real data
bound synthetic share
track data provenance

edge_cases.trigger: synchronous or long-running work runs on the event loop
edge_cases.failure_mode: the loop blocks and all pending tasks stall
edge_cases.example: a synchronous file read freezing the whole async runtime
edge_cases.detection_method: alert on event-loop lag/tick-duration exceeding a threshold
resolution: offload blocking work to a worker pool
make the operation async

edge_cases.trigger: a feedback coupling forms only at runtime via shared state
edge_cases.failure_mode: an unmodeled amplifying loop causes a runaway
edge_cases.example: a shared cache silently coupling two 'isolated' services
edge_cases.detection_method: trace runtime data flow to find couplings absent from the inventory
resolution: add the coupling to the inventory and sign its polarity
break or isolate the shared state

edge_cases.trigger: excessive damping/smoothing is added for stability
edge_cases.failure_mode: the loop becomes sluggish and misses real changes
edge_cases.example: smoothing that delays an autoscaler past the demand spike
edge_cases.detection_method: measure response latency to a step input against the SLO
resolution: reduce damping to the minimum stability margin
re-tune controller gains

workflow.objective: inventory and classify every loop and coupling in the system
acceptance_tests: every executable loop is catalogued with a class tag
each loop has a trigger and period
workflow.do_first_because: every later analysis and fix inherits from a complete, classified loop inventory

workflow.objective: establish correctness, termination, and cost for iterative/recursive loops
acceptance_tests: each loop has a termination proof or an explicit iteration cap
each loop nest has a cost bound
exit_criteria: foundations documented for all catalogued loops
workflow.do_first_because: unbounded or unproven loops are the highest-risk foundation to fix first

workflow.objective: analyze convergence/fixed-point conditions for iterative maps
acceptance_tests: the contraction/stability condition is checked before iterating
a stopping rule is defined
workflow.do_first_because: convergence theory underpins both optimization and damping decisions

workflow.objective: design control-flow and resilience loops with bounds, breakers, and idempotency
entry_criteria: termination caps available for retry loops
acceptance_tests: retries are bounded, jittered, and idempotent
sustained failure trips the breaker
workflow.do_first_because: resilience loops are high-coupling, high-risk and amplify failures if left unbounded

workflow.objective: design the training/eval learning loop with honest signal and rollback
acceptance_tests: train/eval splits are disjoint
a validated regression triggers rollback to a baseline
exit_criteria: learning loop passes eval and rollback acceptance
workflow.do_first_because: learning loops steer the system; a leaked metric or missing rollback bakes in regressions

workflow.objective: map feedback polarity, cascade paths, and self-training collapse risk across loops
acceptance_tests: every coupling is signed with a loop-gain estimate
blast radius is bounded in fault injection
workflow.do_first_because: cross-effects and amplification are the highest-coupling, most irreversible risks

workflow.objective: instrument every loop for health metrics, tracing, and pathology alerts
acceptance_tests: each catalogued loop emits a health metric with an alert
a seeded pathology fires its alert
workflow.do_first_because: you cannot diagnose or verify a stabilization without observing the loop

workflow.objective: decide and plan the stabilization intervention for each diagnosed pathology
acceptance_tests: each intervention is validated against the full coupling map
irreversible fixes carry a decision record
workflow.do_first_because: choosing interventions before global validation risks shifting instability elsewhere

workflow.objective: validate the whole loop design under fault injection and human review of high-risk items
acceptance_tests: fault injection shows bounded blast radius
every high-risk node passed human review
exit_criteria: validation passed and high-risk items reviewed
workflow.do_first_because: irreversible and high-risk loop changes must pass human review before any hard lock

workflow.objective: hard-lock validated loop policies and register change-control triggers
acceptance_tests: all upstream gates and reviews passed before lock
change triggers and downgrade rules are recorded
exit_criteria: loop design hard-locked with change control
workflow.do_first_because: hard lock is only safe after dependency, validation, and human-review gates all pass

priority_rationale.notes: unbounded loops are the top operational risk
convergence theory feeds optimization and damping
the driving loop must be scheduled safely
admission control bounds the retry budget
high-coupling resilience loop that amplifies failures
makes retries/replays safe against double effects
needed to diagnose and verify fixes
final irreversible intervention choice; depends on all analysis

dominance_rules.trigger: a loop fix is rushed past safety analysis
dominance_rules.rule: loop safety (bounds, breakers, rollback) must be in place before shipping a loop change
dominance_rules.required_action: block the change until safety controls are verified
dominance_rules.example: shipping retries with no cap to hit a deadline

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is ordered before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency precedence dominates raw value ordering in execution
dominance_rules.example: scheduling stabilization before the loop inventory

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise score lacks an evidence label
dominance_rules.required_action: attach a heuristic label or downgrade the claim
dominance_rules.example: a 0.91 metric with no source backing

dominance_rules.trigger: a loop policy is about to lock before validation
dominance_rules.rule: validation/QA dominates locking; no hard lock before gates pass
dominance_rules.required_action: hold the lock until fault-injection and review pass
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking a breaker config before injection tests

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible loop change is proposed automatically
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible or high-risk loop changes
dominance_rules.required_action: route the change to human review with a decision record

dominance_rules.trigger: a local loop fix degrades a coupled loop
dominance_rules.rule: global stability across the coupling map dominates a locally optimal fix
dominance_rules.required_action: validate the fix against the full coupling map
dominance_rules.example: more retries fixing one call but amplifying a cascade

dominance_rules.rule: rate limits and breakers dominate retry recovery pressure
dominance_rules.required_action: fit retries inside the protective budget; fail fast otherwise
dominance_rules.example: a retry budget breaching the rate limiter

dominance_rules.trigger: reward proxy rises while true-objective eval falls
dominance_rules.rule: the honest true-objective eval dominates the reward proxy on divergence
dominance_rules.required_action: treat eval as authoritative and revise the reward
dominance_rules.example: optimizing click reward as quality eval drops

dominance_rules.trigger: synthetic data is recycled for scale
dominance_rules.rule: distributional integrity dominates cheap data scale to prevent collapse
dominance_rules.required_action: bound synthetic share and anchor on real data
dominance_rules.example: training mostly on prior model outputs

dominance_rules.trigger: a loop cannot be proven to terminate
dominance_rules.rule: an explicit operational cap plus monitoring dominates unbounded execution where termination is undecidable
dominance_rules.required_action: add an iteration cap and timeout with an alert
dominance_rules.example: an external-input loop with no termination proof

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the loop inventory before fixing any loop
anti_rework_rules.rationale: fixing without a full inventory targets symptoms and misses the driving loop
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a fix proposed for a loop not in the inventory
anti_rework_rules.example: patching a retry without seeing the outer cascade loop

anti_rework_rules.rule: derive competency questions before finalizing nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: questions define what the KB must answer and prevent useless nodes
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: nodes added with no competency-question coverage
anti_rework_rules.example: a node answering no stated question

anti_rework_rules.rule: bound termination before enabling a retry loop
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unbounded retry loop is an outage waiting to happen
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a retry loop shipped without an attempt cap
anti_rework_rules.example: infinite retries against a down dependency

anti_rework_rules.rule: ensure idempotency before retrying side-effecting operations
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: retries enabled on a non-idempotent write

anti_rework_rules.rule: check the convergence condition before tuning the optimizer
anti_rework_rules.rationale: tuning a divergent loop wastes compute and misleads
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: learning rate set without the descent condition
anti_rework_rules.example: an aggressive rate diverging to NaN

anti_rework_rules.rule: secure leakage-free eval before stop/rollback decisions
anti_rework_rules.rationale: stopping or selecting on a leaked metric bakes in the wrong choice
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: checkpoint selected on a leaked eval score
anti_rework_rules.example: rolling back based on an inflated metric

anti_rework_rules.rule: sign feedback polarity before applying damping
anti_rework_rules.rationale: damping the wrong loop wastes margin and leaves the unstable one running
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: damping applied before any polarity analysis
anti_rework_rules.example: smoothing a stable loop while another runs away

anti_rework_rules.rule: size the cascade before choosing a stabilization intervention
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an intervention scoped to one loop can shift instability across the coupling map
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a fix chosen before the cascade path is mapped
anti_rework_rules.example: a local fix ignoring downstream amplification

anti_rework_rules.rule: instrument the loop before deciding and verifying a fix
anti_rework_rules.rationale: fixing blind risks the wrong intervention and unverifiable results
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a stabilization with no metric to confirm it
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning a breaker with no state-transition telemetry

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete validation and human review before hard-locking loop policies
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hard-locking before gates pass makes later fixes expensive change-control events
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock with open high-risk reviews
anti_rework_rules.example: locking a cascade-fix before fault injection

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or design review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and coupling
action: score defects by risk_if_wrong and coupling
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect is addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk warnings remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling or locked node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and couplings of the defect
action: identify dependents via edges and coupling map
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the defect are identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set is stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to its repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: the routed subsystem owns and applies the fix

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changed a node, edge, or score
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and recompute derived fields
acceptance_tests: formula consistency holds within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or an incident updates a prior
iteration_protocol.detection: apply the posterior formula to affected nodes
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed for all affected nodes
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk item cannot be auto-resolved
action: route to human review with a decision record
acceptance_tests: a human decision record exists for the item
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no high-risk item lacks a decision record

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version on the metric suite
action: diff counts and scores vs prior version
acceptance_tests: no metric regresses below the minimum pass condition
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no regression versus the prior version

human_review_required_for: irreversible loop rearchitecture or shared-state breaking
claiming a cascade is bounded without fault injection
hard lock of any loop-stabilization policy
enabling self-training data without provenance anchoring

checks.repair_action: recomputed derived fields via formula tool

test_cases.input_summary: a retry loop with no attempt cap
a partial outage propagates across services
proxy reward rises as quality falls
training on model-generated data over generations

change_triggers: a new loop or coupling is discovered
an incident exceeds the predicted blast radius
an eval metric stops tracking the objective
an oscillation or cascade recurs after a fix
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked loop-policy change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream loop or coupling changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: enabling self-training data without provenance anchoring
hard lock of any loop-stabilization policy
